slice: Fuse same-width small-integer DIV widening into Arrow traversal

scope.runtime: Only same-type Int8/Int8, Int16/Int16 and Int32/Int32 DIV pairs take the new Rust ScalarUDF. It uses existing Arrow try_binary and try_unary to widen each value and write Int64 output in one traversal. DataFusion datum::apply handles scalar/array shapes without expanding scalars to full arrays.
scope.zero_handling: The existing literal-zero path runs first. ANSI uses the existing make_safe_divisor wrapper. Non-ANSI uses the existing NULLIF with a zero of the original input type, avoiding its previous Int32 coercion of Int8/Int16.
scope.simplification: Retain native NULL propagation. A folded same-width literal divisor other than zero or -1 keeps native narrow division and the final Int64 cast, because MIN / -1 is the only overflow at those widths. A scalar -1 uses Arrow unary to widen and negate in one traversal; nonconstant divisors use try_binary or try_unary.
scope.module_placement: The UDF and direct test live in a private sibling module. An earlier inline version changed code generation and slowed an unchanged Decimal control; the separate module recovered its measured performance without changing Decimal arithmetic.
scope.fallback: Mixed integer widths and integer/NULL pairs retain the preceding widening candidate. BIGINT, Decimal, string, floating, interval and other operator paths retain their previous lowering.
scope.benchmark: The preceding 48-case subquery harness and 12-case Float64 harness are unchanged. All three binaries use the identical source and inputs, including the final DECIMAL(38,6) output cast; timings measure the whole projection. No new SQL corpus was needed; reuse the preceding 21 corpora, and extend the Rust boundary check.

provenance.implementation_origin: Local Rust optimization, reusing the existing SparkCheckedDivide scalar/array integration pattern and installed Arrow traversal helpers. No new Sail fix or dependency was imported.
provenance.binary_builds: Original and before binaries are the saved preceding experiment binaries, built with the same 48-case harness. After binaries were rebuilt after adding the Rust tests from the final recorded source. Original is the pre-widening implementation, which fails MIN / -1; before is native Int64 casts; after is this fused candidate.

limitations: The optimization covers only matching Int8, Int16 or Int32 operands. Mixed widths and integer/NULL combinations keep the previous native-cast fallback; their performance is not established by these measurements.

The 12 focused cases cover column divisors and scalar divisor 3. The separate whole-process INT / -1 diagnostic does not establish kernel-only performance or other scalar numerators/divisors and widths.
All 126 tracked value/type or error-stage differences remain, including 11 in the small-integer corpus and 115 in earlier corpora. Counts repeat behaviors across shapes and ANSI modes.

All prior focused error causes, known cause gaps and sort wrappers remain. The invalid value reported first can vary among multiple failing rows in cast corpora; recorded differences retain the same cast failure cause and execution stage.
Numeric comparison covers values, types and coarse error stage, not all schema metadata or structured error conditions. The Delta suite separately checks full schema and rows.

CPU frequency is not fixed and the host is not isolated. Fixed allocator thresholds are diagnostics, not production changes. Timing and user-space counters are separate measurements; counters exclude kernel time during faults.

Default-allocator timing can be bimodal across processes. Preserve slow runs even when the same query is fast in a repeat or under fixed thresholds; reduced arithmetic work is not a guarantee of identical elapsed time in every process.
The Decimal control result is specific to these builds and toolchain. A private module is not a universal guarantee about compiler code generation.
